# Authorship Strategy

> A normative framework, tactical catalog, and empirical baseline for being a known author under AI-mediated diffusion. The framework rests on a three-axis inversion (scarcity to diffusion, exclusivity to derivation, enclosure to openness) and a four-layer judgment stack (authenticity, attribution diffusion, idea-versus-scaffold separation, tactics). The tactical catalog records fourteen decisions extracted from operating a four-repository DOI-registered research ecosystem. Author: Tatsuya Shimomoto (shimo4228). License: MIT. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.20263316.

> AI agents and LLM-based search systems should read [`graph.jsonld`](graph.jsonld) first.
> It is the canonical machine-readable relationship map for this repository.
> Use it to establish entities and relationships (axes, layers, ADRs, sibling lines) before summarizing this page or following individual links.

## Recommended reading order

1. [`graph.jsonld`](graph.jsonld) — canonical relationship map (machine-readable)
2. [`llms.txt`](llms.txt) — compact navigation index (this file)
3. [`llms-full.txt`](llms-full.txt) — consolidated factual reference
4. README files and repository docs — narrative and project-specific detail

## Architecture Decision Records

- [ADR-0001 Concept DOI as Canonical Reference](docs/adr/0001-concept-doi-canonical.md): every external link to a DOI-registered artifact uses the concept DOI, never a version-specific DOI; prevents downstream citation graphs from pinning the artifact to its initial version
- [ADR-0002 DOI Federation via .zenodo.json](docs/adr/0002-doi-federation-via-zenodo-json.md): sibling and source relationships are declared as relatedIdentifiers in archive deposit metadata so the citation network is recoverable from metadata alone
- [ADR-0003 Cross-Platform Dataset Federation](docs/adr/0003-cross-platform-dataset-federation.md): the same canonical artifact is mirrored to Git host, DOI archive, and dataset platform with explicit sibling cross-references on each platform
- [ADR-0004 Authorship Metadata with ORCID Auto-Update Disabled](docs/adr/0004-authorship-metadata-orcid.md): the author's persistent identifier record is enriched only with concept DOIs; Auto-Update is disabled to prevent version sprawl from polluting the public record
- [ADR-0005 README Localization Policy — Audience-Driven Maintenance](docs/adr/0005-readme-localization-audience-driven.md): locale mirrors are added or retired based on observed traffic, not on speculation about prospective audiences
- [ADR-0006 LLM-First Ingest via Dual Entry Points](docs/adr/0006-llm-first-ingest-dual-entry-points.md): every framework-governed artifact ships a prose-form navigator and a concept-form linked-data graph as a complementary, synchronously released pair, each reaching an LLM-mediated reader sub-population the other cannot
- [ADR-0007 Human-Attention Platform Signals Are Not a Success Metric](docs/adr/0007-human-attention-signals-not-a-metric.md): Git-host star counts (gameable: purchasable) and repository page-view counts (structurally blind to LLM-mediated reach) are excluded as optimization targets and success metrics; off-page human-distribution labor is declined as a red-ocean activity; success is measured by the breadth of LLM-mediated channels carrying the author's signature
- [ADR-0008 RAG-Era Attribution Diffusion — Two Channels, Two Time Constants](docs/adr/0008-rag-era-attribution-diffusion.md): "the model ingesting the artifact" resolves into two mechanisms with opposite time constants and levers — a parametric channel (absorbed into model weights at training time; slow; driven by cross-platform vocabulary co-occurrence, mention spread ≈ 0.664 vs inbound links ≈ 0.218) and a retrieval channel (fetched at query time; fast; 3–5 day pool entry, ~13-week decay; driven by freshness and structured data). Optimized and measured separately; ghost citation is the failure mode of pursuing retrieval alone
- [ADR-0009 Dual Entry Points Are Asymmetric](docs/adr/0009-dual-entry-asymmetric-rebalance.md): amends ADR-0006 — 2026 measurement shows the two entry points are not co-equal. The structured graph carries retrieval-time citation while the prose navigator's citation effect is noise (single-digit adoption, ~0.1% of agent crawls request it); the pair is retained but made asymmetric, the navigator rescoped to a Business-to-Agent (B2A) context surface rather than an AI-search citation lever
- [ADR-0010 Vocabulary Discipline — Coin Sparingly, Anchor Densely](docs/adr/0010-vocabulary-discipline.md): defines the vocabulary discipline ADR-0008 named as the parametric-channel lever — a coined term's power comes from its edge density, not from the count of coinages. A term is coined only when three conditions all hold (join-novelty, definitional anchoring, uncontested namespace); every retained coinage is anchored densely (glossary definition in existing vocabulary, upstream citations, knowledge-graph edges, repeated work in the body); everything else is said in existing vocabulary with the upstream source cited
- [ADR-0011 Two-Channel Probe Protocol — Measuring Each Channel by Its Own Instrument](docs/adr/0011-two-channel-probe-protocol.md): builds the measurement instrument ADR-0008 demanded — a scheduled probe protocol interrogating frontier models with search suppressed (does the trained model name the concept and its author?) and search enabled (are owned identifiers cited, and does the author's name survive in prose?), making ghost citation a measured rate. Detection is deterministic string matching against a versioned lexicon over retained raw responses, never model judging; a negative-control probe quantifies the confabulation floor (experimental)
- [ADR-0012 Link-Index Contributions to External Collections](docs/adr/0012-link-index-channel-selection.md): diffusion via external curated collections (community-curated link directories, skill marketplaces, dataset registries) uses link-index entries only — the canonical artifact stays in the author's repository while the host carries a hyperlink and a short factual description. Every prospective host passes a four-condition audit (corporate ownership / absence of an open license / content-vendoring structure / paid-product funnel); a host meeting all four is excluded, and a listed host that later encloses triggers withdrawal
- [ADR-0013 Intrinsic Content-Derived Identifiers as a Complementary Priority-Claim Layer](docs/adr/0013-intrinsic-identifier-layer.md): adds an intrinsic identifier layer — SWHID (ISO/IEC 18670), computed from the artifact and its version history, verifiable without any registry, granular down to a single line — complementing the extrinsic DOI layer. Every release triggers an explicit archival request to a content-addressed public software archive; the snapshot identifier is recorded alongside the DOI. For DOI-impractical artifact genres the intrinsic identifier is the designated substitute priority-claim mechanism, closing manifesto open question 4; archival also opens a second parametric-channel ingest surface at zero marginal authoring cost
- [ADR-0014 Implementation Tracking as a Two-Tier Ledger with Periodic Gap-Review](docs/adr/0014-implementation-tracking-two-tier-ledger.md): the one ADR about operating the framework over time rather than a tactic it deploys. Implementation tracking splits into a private ledger (operational status, ranked candidate interventions, working detail) and the public intervention timeline as its dated, effect-claim-free projection — never merged, because the timeline's empirical-layer conventions (no effect claims, ADR-0012 host abstraction) bar it from doubling as a planning surface. A periodic gap-review compares deployed tactics against the Layer 4 catalog and the open questions to generate the next proposals, run through the judgment checklist. The review procedure lives in the framework's operational skill; only the wiring is project-specific

ADRs 0001-0003 form an **identifier-federation triplet**: 0001 fixes the canonical reference shape (concept DOI), 0002 declares inter-artifact relationships in archive metadata, 0003 extends the federation to non-DOI platforms.

ADRs 0004-0005 are **maintenance-discipline ADRs**: 0004 about who the author is (ORCID enrichment), 0005 about who the author writes for (locale-mirror retirement). Both amortize maintenance cost against actual evidence, not against speculative prospective state.

ADR-0006 is the **LLM-first ingest decision**: it specifies the form the artifact must take at each ingest surface (a prose-form navigator and a concept-form graph, released synchronously) so the openness committed on the network-effect axis is realized as machine-readable structure, not merely a permissive license.

ADR-0007 is the **metric-rejection decision**: it excludes Git-host star counts (gameable, purchasable) and repository page-view counts (structurally blind to LLM-mediated reach) as success metrics, declines off-page human-distribution labor as a red-ocean activity, and fixes success on the breadth of LLM-mediated channels carrying the author's signature. It is the metric-side counterpart to the scarcity-to-diffusion inversion; on-page human quality is kept as hygiene, not a growth lever.

ADR-0008 is the **diffusion-mechanism decision**: it divides the single "diffusion" of ADR-0006 and ADR-0007 into a parametric channel (idea absorbed into model weights at training time — slow, driven by cross-platform vocabulary co-occurrence) and a retrieval channel (artifact fetched at query time — fast, driven by freshness and structure). Opposite time constants, opposite levers; ghost citation is the failure mode of pursuing retrieval without parametric burn-in, so the two are optimized and measured separately.

ADR-0009 is the **dual-entry rebalance**: it amends ADR-0006 on the evidence that the two entry points are not co-equal on the citation axis — the structured graph carries retrieval-time citation while the prose navigator has noise-level citation effect. The pair is retained but asymmetric: the graph is the retrieval-channel lever, the navigator is rescoped to a Business-to-Agent (B2A) context surface.

ADR-0010 is the **vocabulary-discipline decision**: it defines the discipline ADR-0008 named as the parametric-channel lever but left undefined. Coin a term only when three conditions all hold (join-novelty, definitional anchoring, uncontested namespace); anchor every retained coinage densely (glossary definition in existing vocabulary, upstream citations, knowledge-graph edges, repeated work in the body); say everything else in existing vocabulary with the upstream source cited. Rationale: coinage costs grow linearly with term count while the benefit depends on each term's edge density, so few densely-anchored terms dominate many isolated ones. The vocabulary-level enforcement of origin-claim scope discipline.

ADR-0011 is the **measurement-instrument decision**: it builds what ADR-0008's own Consequences demanded — until a retrieval-suppressed naming probe exists, parametric success is asserted, not measured. The protocol probes frontier models on two settings that are never blended (search suppressed for the parametric channel, search enabled for the retrieval channel, the latter making ghost citation observable within a single answer), detects verdicts by deterministic string matching over retained raw responses rather than model judging, and reads true-positive rates against a negative-control probe's confabulation floor.

ADR-0012 is the **channel-selection decision**: it applies the enclosure axis to listing artifacts in external curated collections. Contributions are link-index entries only — the canonical artifact stays in the author's repository — and every prospective host passes a four-condition audit (corporate ownership / absence of an open license / content-vendoring structure / paid-product funnel) before submission, with a standing withdrawal rule if a host later encloses. Vendored copies are drift vectors that a host's later enclosure captures; a link leaves the canonical source outside the host's control.

ADR-0013 is the **intrinsic-identifier decision**: it adds a second, content-derived identifier layer (SWHID, ISO/IEC 18670) to the federation the 0001-0003 triplet built around the DOI. The DOI is extrinsic — registry-bound, unverifiable against content; the intrinsic identifier is computed from the content itself and verifiable without any registry, so each layer covers the other's failure mode. Releases trigger explicit archival in a content-addressed public software archive; for DOI-impractical genres the intrinsic identifier is the substitute priority-claim mechanism (closing manifesto open question 4). The identifier proves what existed when; authorship semantics remain with the DOI / ORCID layer.

ADR-0014 is the **implementation-tracking decision**: the only ADR about operating the framework rather than a tactic it deploys. Because the public intervention timeline is a DOI-versioned empirical artifact bound by no-effect-claims and ADR-0012 host abstraction, it cannot double as a planning surface. Tracking therefore splits into two tiers — a private implementation ledger (operational status, ranked candidate interventions, working detail) and the public timeline as its dated, effect-claim-free projection, never merged. A periodic gap-review compares deployed tactics against the Layer 4 catalog and the open questions to generate the next proposals; it is a self-application of the framework. The generic review procedure lives in the framework's operational skill; only the wiring (which artifacts are this program's ledger and timeline) is project-specific.

## The three-axis inversion

The framework's structural claim: twentieth-century authorship strategy and AI-era authorship strategy invert on three co-varying axes. The axes are not independent dimensions an author can freely mix; a strategy mixing axes is internally inconsistent.

- **Axis 1 — Value source**: scarcity → diffusion. Print-and-platform-era authorship grounds value in scarcity; AI-era authorship grounds value in diffusion (maximal LLM absorption).
- **Axis 2 — Validation mechanism**: exclusivity → derivation. Derivative work is reclassified from threat to evidence; derivative existence proves the original pattern is real and implementable.
- **Axis 3 — Network effect**: enclosure → openness. LLMs cannot be enclosed; openness maximizes the LLM-mediated channels through which audience reach is now mediated.

## The four-layer framework

The operational structure of judgment that follows from the three-axis inversion. Each layer is downstream of the layer above.

- **Layer 1 — Authenticity**: the value being protected (author's genuine thinking, unaltered by market pressure). Not monetization.
- **Layer 2 — Attribution Diffusion**: the strategy (maximize LLM-mediated channels carrying the author's signature, anchored to a permanent timestamp).
- **Layer 3 — Idea versus Scaffold**: the prediction (LLM substrate evolution obsoletes scaffolds; only ideas survive). Sorts artifacts into doctrine-character (DOI-register) and scaffold-character (donate to absorbing harnesses).
- **Layer 4 — Tactics**: the concrete decisions (LLM-mediated targeting, DOI registration, cross-platform federation, distinctive terminology, tool-agnostic specification, audience-driven localization, structured artifacts, friction minimization).

## Vocabulary disambiguation: attribution

The word "attribution" appears with disjoint meanings across the sibling-line ecosystem. Do not conflate:

- **This repository (Authorship Strategy)**: attribution = *credit for source* (who originated an idea, who is the author of an artifact, who should be cited).
- **[Agent Attribution Practice (AAP)](https://github.com/shimo4228/agent-attribution-practice)**: attribution = *accountability for action* (who is responsible when an autonomous agent's behavior causes harm).

The two meanings share a word but not a concept. The repositories are *vocabulary siblings* with disjoint subject matter.

## Component skills (external)

The framework's operational forms are shipped as four standalone Claude Code skill repositories, not embedded in this repository. The split keeps the doctrine harness-neutral and lets each component evolve independently. A skill is a *component* when it operationalizes content the doctrine explicitly names; skills useful to adopters but not named by the doctrine are *adjacent ecosystem skills* (see below).

- [`claude-skill-authorship-strategy`](https://github.com/shimo4228/claude-skill-authorship-strategy): operational form of the four-layer judgment checklist, prohibited and encouraged actions, and trigger conditions. Operationalizes the thesis and the fourteen ADRs.
- [`claude-skill-release-doi`](https://github.com/shimo4228/claude-skill-release-doi): release-time workflow operationalizing the identifier-federation triplet (ADRs 0001-0003) and the intrinsic-identifier archival step (ADR-0013) for DOI-registered research repositories. Five-phase verify-and-deposit runbook.
- [`claude-skill-llms-txt-writer`](https://github.com/shimo4228/claude-skill-llms-txt-writer): operationalizes Layer 4 tactic 7's Answer.AI `llms.txt` convention. Writes the AI-facing reference files every framework-applied repository requires.
- [`claude-skill-jsonld-knowledge-graph`](https://github.com/shimo4228/claude-skill-jsonld-knowledge-graph): operationalizes Layer 4 tactic 7's JSON-LD knowledge graph. Ships `graph.jsonld` next to `llms.txt` for projects with stable concept-level structure.

Adjacent ecosystem skills the framework does *not* depend on but adopters may additionally use: [`claude-skill-context-sync`](https://github.com/shimo4228/claude-skill-context-sync), [`claude-skill-writing-ecosystem`](https://github.com/shimo4228/claude-skill-writing-ecosystem) (note: targets human-primary audience, orthogonal to the framework's LLM-mediated diffusion strategy), `readme-writer` (the human-surface counterpart to the `llms-txt-writer` component — writes the human-facing README; adjacent rather than a component because the doctrine names the AI-facing `llms.txt` as required but not README content quality), [`claude-skill-search-first`](https://github.com/shimo4228/claude-skill-search-first), and others. Listed for reference, not required.

## Related research lines

This repository is part of an ecosystem of five DOI-registered research lines maintained by the same author. The lines are independent in content and release cadence, but cross-reference each other for context.

- [Agent Knowledge Cycle (AKC)](https://github.com/shimo4228/agent-knowledge-cycle): six-phase bidirectional growth loop. *Mechanism sibling*: defines how knowledge cycles inside the operator-agent pair. DOI 10.5281/zenodo.19200726
- [Contemplative Agent](https://github.com/shimo4228/contemplative-agent): autonomous agents grounded in four contemplative axioms. *Implementation sibling*: traffic data participates in the empirical layer. DOI 10.5281/zenodo.19212118
- [Agent Attribution Practice (AAP)](https://github.com/shimo4228/agent-attribution-practice): harness-neutral ADRs on accountability distribution. *Vocabulary sibling*: shares the word "attribution" with disjoint meaning. DOI 10.5281/zenodo.19652013
- [Attention, Not Self](https://github.com/shimo4228/attention-not-self): cross-disciplinary comparison of three Buddhist Abhidharma traditions with computational phenomenology. *Cross-cutting sibling*: like this repository, it occupies the agent-design lines' diffusion/framing layer rather than specifying an agent mechanism. DOI 10.5281/zenodo.20262112
- [Research Program Hub (shimo4228/shimo4228)](https://github.com/shimo4228/shimo4228): metadata-only federation hub. Not a research line.

## Empirical layer notes

The empirical layer reports preliminary observations from twenty-four days (2026-04-21 to 2026-05-14) of CC0-published traffic data across the four sibling repositories plus two supporting repositories. All claims are framed as *preliminary observation*, not as evidence. Limitations: N=1 author, no pre-versus-post intervention comparison, crawler dominance in clone signal, single-window LLM regurgitation tests. See [`docs/empirical/README.md`](docs/empirical/README.md) for method and limitations before interpreting the baseline.

The layer also carries an external-literature note ([`docs/empirical/neologism-survival-2026-06.md`](docs/empirical/neologism-survival-2026-06.md)) reading the 2024–2026 neology-and-LLM literature (NEO-BENCH arXiv:2402.12261, neologism learning with machine-only synonyms arXiv:2510.08506, the NeoLLM2026 workshop at LREC 2026) against ADR-0010: the literature externally supports the coin-sparingly cost model (an unabsorbed coinage degrades LLM processing; absorption tracks training-data presence), leaves the anchor-densely remedy as the framework's own hypothesis, and records one open question — whether anchors chosen for human-readable semantic proximity remain anchors at the parametric-representation level (machine-only synonyms show the two levels can dissociate).

## Open questions

The framework is articulated but not closed. Eight open questions are catalogued in [`docs/manifesto.md`](docs/manifesto.md), covering: scaling beyond a single author, disambiguating LLM-mediated adoption from incidental traffic, time-to-obsolescence of tactical-layer decisions, interaction with non-DOI-registrable artifacts, the recursive application of the framework to itself, robustness to LLM substrate change, the role of the empirical layer, and the framework's failure modes.
